instructions: If invoice line 3 ("VULN-DASH™ Portal Access — 4 named seats (H. Te Whaiti, J. Prasad, M. Liu, S. Burrows), July 2026") bills work or goods: what do OUR OWN records establish about whether it was performed or delivered for the billed period? Pick one. The vendor's own documents never move a line out of vendor_only.

criteria.confirmed: confirmed: OUR OWN records (a goods receipt, receiving confirmation, acceptance record, owner tracker note, owner comment or an unqualified owner approval) say the work or goods on invoice line 3 ("VULN-DASH™ Portal Access — 4 named seats (H. Te Whaiti, J. Prasad, M. Liu, S. Burrows), July 2026") were delivered or performed as billed for the billed period or milestone, or delivered with only the formal sign-off still pending. A record that describes the deliverable as a whole confirms every line of it. When our records disagree, the acceptance record, then the goods receipt, governs the count and an owner note governs degree and quality. NO if our record says less or nothing was done, if only the vendor's own documents describe it, or if nothing describes it. A record describing the deliverable or service period as a whole confirms every line the packet places within it, including hourly or add-on lines for that period, unless it names the line's work as missing or incomplete; a record that itemises what it reviewed confirms only the items it names, and a record that names the period or deliverable and then lists what it comprised or what was checked IS an itemising record. Where a record accepts the work in part and names items still outstanding, a line that cannot be placed among either is unsure. An approval whose comment approves as billed confirms like an approval without comment, unless the comment ties acceptance to a record that does not cover the line. A delivered item with a minor, remediable defect is confirmed. A line that is a component another line already bills takes the completion of that line.
criteria.less: less: OUR OWN record says LESS was done or delivered on invoice line 3 ("VULN-DASH™ Portal Access — 4 named seats (H. Te Whaiti, J. Prasad, M. Liu, S. Burrows), July 2026") than the line bills: a lower percent complete, fewer units or a smaller headcount, components not fitted, deliverables the owner says are missing, receiving short (an acceptance record, or a goods receipt when there is no acceptance record). Only the buyer's own words count. When our records disagree, the acceptance record, then the goods receipt, governs the count and an owner note governs degree and quality; a goods receipt plainly wrong for lines other records verify is disregarded. NO if our record says nothing was done at all, if the disagreement is about whether the work was AUTHORISED (scope) or about price, or if the only conflicting document is the vendor's. Also YES for a deliverable our record says was delivered but nonconforming or requiring revision before acceptance. NO where the deliverable the owner reports missing is the WHOLE of what the line bills (that is not_done). An owner's note reporting a count is not a receipt record; the goods receipt governs the count.
criteria.not_done: not_done: Our own records, or the vendor's own admission in the thread, say the work or goods on invoice line 3 ("VULN-DASH™ Portal Access — 4 named seats (H. Te Whaiti, J. Prasad, M. Liu, S. Burrows), July 2026") have NOT HAPPENED AT ALL: not started, nothing delivered, milestone not reached. Partly done, done differently, fewer units or a lower percent complete is NO (that is 'less'). A milestone billed before its acceptance with no record saying the work has not happened is NO. A single deliverable that the owner's record says has not been received is not_done, not less.
criteria.vendor_only: vendor_only: The ONLY evidence describing the work or goods on invoice line 3 ("VULN-DASH™ Portal Access — 4 named seats (H. Te Whaiti, J. Prasad, M. Liu, S. Burrows), July 2026") is the vendor's own: its service log, its report, its delivery note, its timesheet. Nothing from our side (receipt, receiving, acceptance, owner note or an approval without comment) describes this line's work as delivered, short or not done. NO only if such a record of ours exists (a note that our review is still pending is not one), or if nothing at all describes it. The vendor's own evidence includes a timesheet or transmittal reproduced on or attached to the invoice, and the vendor's assertion in an email or in the invoice's own narrative that the work was performed. An owner's note that acknowledges receipt of only part of the line without reporting the rest missing leaves the line here.
criteria.none: none: NOTHING in the packet describes the work or goods on invoice line 3 ("VULN-DASH™ Portal Access — 4 named seats (H. Te Whaiti, J. Prasad, M. Liu, S. Burrows), July 2026") as delivered or performed for the billed period: no record of ours and no vendor document either. Unqualified owner approval of the invoice counts as our record (then NO). A record describing a deliverable as a whole confirms only lines the packet places within that deliverable; a line the packet does not so place, described nowhere but by its own text and amount, is none.
criteria.unsure: unsure: UNSURE: none of the other options is more likely than not; the packet genuinely supports two of them. Not a way to defer a decision you could make.

contract.title: Subscription Agreement AGR-2026-09 — Continuous Penetration Testing & Vulnerability Assessment Services
relevant_excerpts: 2. Scope of Services. 2.1 SecureEdge shall provide the Customer with continuous penetration testing and vulnerability assessment services ('Services') targeting the Customer's external and internal network infrastructure, web applications (including the GrantsHub™ portal and DonorConnect interface), and API integration endpoints, as further described in Schedule A. 2.2 Services include automated vulnerability scanning, manual penetration testing, reporting of findings classified per CVSS v3.1, and remediation-validation re-testing upon Customer request. 2.3 The Customer shall consume Services on a metered basis; usage shall be measured in scan-hours (automated scanning engine time) and test-units (each discrete manual test engagement of up to four hours' duration). 2.4 Services expressly exclude red-team physical intrusion testing, social-engineering campaigns, and any testing of third-party hosted SaaS platforms not contractually controlled by the Customer, unless agreed via a Change Order under clause 9.

4. Fees and Invoicing. 4.1 The Customer shall pay for Services consumed during each calendar month in arrears, at the rates set out in Schedule B (Rate Card). 4.2 SecureEdge shall issue a tax invoice by the twentieth (20th) day of the month following the metering period, itemising scan-hours and test-units consumed, with supporting usage logs exported from the VULN-DASH™ portal. 4.3 Invoices are payable within thirty (30) days of the invoice date. 4.4 Total fees payable under this Agreement shall not exceed the Purchase Order ceiling of AUD 87,100.00 (inclusive of GST) without prior written approval from the Customer's authorised procurement delegate. 4.5 Where metered consumption in any month would cause aggregate billings to exceed ninety percent (90%) of the PO ceiling, SecureEdge shall notify the Customer's nominated contract manager within two (2) business days.

5. Acceptance. 5.1 Each penetration test report and vulnerability scan summary ('Deliverable') shall be deemed accepted unless the Customer provides written notice of material deficiency within ten (10) business days of delivery via the VULN-DASH™ portal or email to the designated SecureEdge engagement lead. 5.2 Material deficiency is limited to: (a) failure to test the agreed-scope targets; (b) misclassification of findings by two or more CVSS severity bands; or (c) inclusion of data from environments outside the authorised test scope. 5.3 Upon receipt of a deficiency notice, SecureEdge shall remediate and re-deliver within five (5) business days at no additional charge.

9. Changes. 9.1 Either party may propose changes to the scope, rate card, or consumption limits by issuing a written Change Order request referencing this Agreement (AGR-2026-09). 9.2 No Change Order shall be effective unless signed by both parties' authorised representatives. 9.3 Work performed outside the scope defined in clause 2 without an executed Change Order shall not be billable and shall be performed at SecureEdge's own risk. 9.4 If the Customer requests services that SecureEdge reasonably determines fall outside scope, SecureEdge shall promptly notify the Customer in writing (referencing the relevant support ticket) before commencing any such work.

Fees and Invoicing. 4.1 The Customer shall pay for Services consumed during each calendar month in arrears, at the rates set out in Schedule B (Rate Card). 4.2 SecureEdge shall issue a tax invoice by the twentieth (20th) day of the month following the metering period, itemising scan-hours and test-units consumed, with supporting usage logs exported from the VULN-DASH™ portal. 4.3 Invoices are payable within thirty (30) days of the invoice date. 4.4 Total fees payable under this Agreement shall not exceed the Purchase Order ceiling of AUD 87,100.00 (inclusive of GST) without prior written approval from the Customer's authorised procurement delegate. 4.5 Where metered consumption in any month would cause aggregate billings to exceed ninety percent (90%) of the PO ceiling, SecureEdge shall notify the Customer's nominated contract manager within two (2) business days.

5. Acceptance. 5.1 Each penetration test report and vulnerability scan summary ('Deliverable') shall be deemed accepted unless the Customer provides written notice of material deficiency within ten (10) business days of delivery via the VULN-DASH™ portal or email to the designated SecureEdge engagement lead. 5.2 Material deficiency is limited to: (a) failure to test the agreed-scope targets; (b) misclassification of findings by two or more CVSS severity bands; or (c) inclusion of data from environments outside the authorised test scope. 5.3 Upon receipt of a deficiency notice, SecureEdge shall remediate and re-deliver within five (5) business days at no additional charge.

9. Changes. 9.1 Either party may propose changes to the scope, rate card, or consumption limits by issuing a written Change Order request referencing this Agreement (AGR-2026-09). 9.2 No Change Order shall be effective unless signed by both parties' authorised representatives. 9.3 Work performed outside the scope defined in clause 2 without an executed Change Order shall not be billable and shall be performed at SecureEdge's own risk. 9.4 If the Customer requests services that SecureEdge reasonably determines fall outside scope, SecureEdge shall promptly notify the Customer in writing (referencing the relevant support ticket) before commencing any such work.

instructions: Invoice line 1 ("Automated Scan-Hours — Internal Network Vulnerability Scanning (Corporate Services VLANs CS-01–CS-04), July 2026 cycle, ref SEC-2026-0148") is an ADD-ON charge rather than the work or goods themselves: a fee, surcharge, handling, admin, expediting, minimum-charge or adjustment line (a 'coordination fee', not coordination labour on site) that sits on top of the priced work and traces to no PO line, no contract clause, and not to how this vendor has billed before (see prior invoices). A line billing services or goods is NOT a fee however vague its wording ("Consulting services", "Professional fees", "Work performed"); vagueness is a separate question. A credit, discount or rebate line, even shown as a positive amount, is never a fee (it is an adjustment); a tax or expense line is not a fee. Fees the contract or PO text provides for, and charges a PO line prices, are explained; scope prose is not a PO line. A commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines is a charge on top, explained where the contract provides for it.

state.passage: The Genetic Code To summarize what we know to this point, the cellular process of transcription generates messenger RNA (mRNA), a mobile molecular copy of one or more genes with an alphabet of A, C, G, and uracil (U). Translation of the mRNA template converts nucleotide-based genetic information into a protein product. Protein sequences consist of 20 commonly occurring amino acids; therefore, it can be said that the protein alphabet consists of 20 letters. Each amino acid is defined by a threenucleotide sequence called the triplet codon. The relationship between a nucleotide codon and its corresponding amino acid is called the genetic code. Given the different numbers of “letters” in the mRNA and protein “alphabets,” combinations of nucleotides corresponded to single amino acids. Using a three-nucleotide code means that there are a total of 64 (4 × 4 × 4) possible combinations; therefore, a given amino acid is encoded by more than one nucleotide triplet (Figure 9.20).
